S3a port (sync-main1): D324's elevated default DACL (main, kept) gives the sandbox users' group GENERIC_ALL and the sandbox account, OWNER RIGHTS, the logon SID, Everyone and the capability SIDs GENERIC_READ|GENERIC_EXECUTE. Read checks use normal SIDs, so any elevated command (any logon of the sandbox account) can read another one's processes, which upstream's #47361 forbids for its shared DACL (logon SID only). Same as main; stricter than upstream on writes between commands of one logon, looser on reads across logons. No production builder uses upstream's Shared DACL. S3b decides whether elevated commands should drop read access for the group and shared SIDs (cf. D429 for legacy).

S3a port (sync-main1): #1810 test expectation changed: upstream's protocol marks the legacy-format profiles with a writable folder inside .git/.codex/.agents (and .git itself writable) as needing direct runtime enforcement; the three refusals still hold. S3b confirms the direct-enforcement path also refuses them on Windows.

S3a port review (sync-main1): main's world-writable scan (deny-write ACEs for the capability SIDs on Everyone-writable folders, called at TUI startup) is gone on the sync branch since S3a took upstream's deletion (#47943). The legacy token still has Everyone as a restricting SID, so without the scan an Everyone-writable folder stays writable from the legacy sandbox. S3b decides: restore audit.rs (with main's #1871/#1805 edits) and its TUI call, or accept upstream's removal with sign-off. Main's callers: tui/src/app/platform_actions.rs and tui/src/chatwidget/windows_sandbox_prompts.rs:56 (S4a/S4b); tui/src/app.rs still calls the undefined spawn_world_writable_scan since the skeleton, so the Windows TUI won't compile until S4a resolves it.

S3a port review (sync-main1): D283's exemption (no default .git/.codex/.agents protection in temp roots) is gone since S3a took upstream's :tmpdir resolution; temp roots now get the defaults (stricter), and TEMP/TMP naming one folder give one root. S3b decides whether to restore D283's exemption or accept upstream's (Decision for Travis).

S3a port review (sync-main1): add_deny_ace opens with FILE_FLAG_OPEN_REPARSE_POINT for every deny kind, as main's SetNamedSecurityInfoW wrote a link itself (D352). Upstream's deny-read path is not weakened: deny_read_acl.rs uses main's add_deny_read_ace_to_object (follows links, records the object), and add_deny_read_ace has no non-test caller. Carried-over gap, same as main: if codex_home is itself a junction, the ReadNewFiles deny lands on the junction, and has_deny_read_ace_for_new_files (no-follow) agrees, so the launch proceeds. Also inherited: add_required_deny_write_ace, add_deny_delete_ace and ensure_explicit_deny_read_ace verify through fetch_dacl_handle, which follows links (fails closed on a link). S3b decides whether to close the junction-home case.
